In the evening the stars appear.
It is already time to leave.
exFr: Il est déjà l'heure de partir.

exEn: For many years! (a blessing)
exFr: Pour de longues années ! (vœu de bonheur)

exEn: The month has thirty days.

ex: Ἐν τῷ θέρει ἡ γῆ καρποὺς φέρει.
exEn: In summer the earth bears fruit.
exFr: En été, la terre porte ses fruits.

ex: Μετὰ τὸν χειμῶνα τὸ ἔαρ ἔρχεται.
exEn: After winter comes spring.
One swallow does not make a spring.
exFr: Une hirondelle ne fait pas le printemps.

ex: Ὁ ἀνεξέταστος βίος οὐ βιωτὸς ἀνθρώπῳ.
exEn: The unexamined life is not worth living for a human being.
exFr: Une vie sans examen ne vaut pas d'être vécue.

exEn: Life is short, but sweet.
exFr: La vie est brève, mais douce.

ex: Σῖτος καὶ ὕδωρ ἀναγκαῖα τῷ βίῳ.
exEn: Grain and water are necessary for life.
exFr: Le blé et l'eau sont nécessaires à la vie.

ex: Οὐκ ἐπ' ἄρτῳ μόνῳ ζήσεται ἄνθρωπος.
exEn: Man shall not live by bread alone.
exFr: L'homme ne vivra pas de pain seulement.

exEn: In wine there is truth.
The baby drinks milk.
His voice flowed sweeter than honey.
exFr: Sa voix coulait plus douce que le miel.

exEn: You are pouring oil on the fire.
exFr: Tu verses de l'huile sur le feu.

exEn: The olive tree is Athena's gift.
The shepherd makes cheese.
At the festival we eat meat.
exFr: Pendant la fête, nous mangeons de la viande.

exEn: I invite you to dinner.
In winter we wear a thick cloak.
exFr: En hiver, nous portons un manteau épais.

exEn: The tunic is white.

ex: Τὸ βιβλίον ὥσπερ φίλος πιστός ἐστιν.
exEn: A book is like a faithful friend.
exFr: Un livre est comme un ami fidèle.

ex: Τὰ γράμματα μένει, οἱ δὲ λόγοι πέτονται.
exEn: Writings remain, spoken words fly away.
exFr: Les écrits restent, les paroles s'envolent.

exEn: I receive a letter from my friend.
exFr: Je reçois une lettre de mon ami.

ex: Φοβοῦ τοὺς Δαναοὺς καὶ δῶρα φέροντας.
exEn: Beware of Greeks even bearing gifts.
exFr: Crains les Grecs, même porteurs de présents.

exEn: I have money in my purse.
exFr: J'ai de l'argent dans ma bourse.

exEn: The worker is worthy of his wage.
A possession for all time.
Work is no disgrace.
exFr: Le travail n'est pas une honte.

ex: Τῶν πόνων πωλοῦσιν ἡμῖν πάντα τἀγαθὰ οἱ θεοί.
exEn: The gods sell us all good things at the price of toil.
exFr: Les dieux nous vendent tous les biens au prix de la peine.

exEn: The matter speaks for itself.
Our country is beautiful.
This place is sacred.

ex: Ὁ κόσμος σκηνή, ὁ βίος πάροδος.
exEn: The world is a stage, life is a passing entrance.
exFr: Le monde est une scène, la vie un passage.

exEn: The human race is one.
Plato speaks about the Forms.
Great is the power of truth.
exFr: Grande est la puissance de la vérité.

ex: Τρόπος ἐστὶν ὁ πείθων, οὐ λόγος.
exEn: It is character that persuades, not speech.
exFr: C'est le caractère qui persuade, non le discours.

exEn: Each person is a part of the city.
exFr: Chacun est une partie de la cité.

ex: Τὸ πλῆθος ἐν τῇ ἀγορᾷ συλλέγεται.
exEn: The crowd gathers in the marketplace.
exFr: La foule se rassemble sur l'agora.

exEn: All is number.
Man is the measure of all things.
exFr: L'homme est la mesure de toutes choses.

ex: Ὁ πλοῦτος ἄνευ ἀρετῆς οὐδὲν ὠφελεῖ.
exEn: Wealth without virtue is of no benefit.
exFr: La richesse sans la vertu ne sert à rien.

exEn: Poverty awakens the arts.

ex: Ἡ νόσος τὸ σῶμα ἀσθενὲς ποιεῖ.
exEn: Disease makes the body weak.
Speech is a remedy for grief.
exFr: La parole est un remède au chagrin.

exEn: Health is the greatest of goods.
exFr: La santé est le plus grand des biens.

exEn: She has tears in her eyes.
exFr: Elle a des larmes dans les yeux.

exEn: Unquenchable laughter among the gods.
exFr: Un rire inextinguible chez les dieux.

exEn: You are singing a beautiful song.
Music educates the soul.

ex: Ὁ χορὸς ἐν τῷ θεάτρῳ ᾄδει.
exEn: The chorus sings in the theater.
The contest admits no excuses.
The beginning is half of the whole.
exFr: Commencer, c'est déjà la moitié du tout.

exEn: Look to the end of life.
exFr: Regarde la fin de la vie.

exEn: Sing, goddess, the wrath.
Kindness gives birth to kindness.
exFr: Une grâce en engendre une autre.

exEn: A gentleman, beautiful and good.
exFr: Un homme accompli, beau et bon.

exEn: From a bad crow, a bad egg.
exFr: D'un mauvais corbeau, un mauvais œuf.

exEn: Beautiful things are difficult.
Lying is shameful.
Big book, big evil.
From a small seed, a great tree.
exFr: D'une petite graine, un grand arbre.

ex: Πολλαὶ χεῖρες τὸ ἔργον ἐλαφρὸν ποιοῦσιν.
exEn: Many hands make the work light.
exFr: Beaucoup de mains rendent le travail léger.

ex: Πολλοὶ μὲν κλητοί, ὀλίγοι δὲ ἐκλεκτοί.
exEn: Many are called, but few are chosen.
Practice is everything.
The wise man is never alone.
Different people say different things.
The young learn quickly.

ex: Ὁ παλαιὸς οἶνος ἡδίων τοῦ νέου.
exEn: Old wine is sweeter than new.
exFr: Le vin vieux est plus doux que le nouveau.

exEn: To a wise man every land is open.
exFr: Pour l'homme sage, toute terre est praticable.

ex: Δίκαιος ἴσθι καὶ πρὸς τοὺς ἐχθρούς.
exEn: Be just even toward your enemies.
exFr: Sois juste même envers tes ennemis.

exEn: What you say is true.
Necessity is strongest, for it rules everything.
exFr: La nécessité est la plus forte, car elle commande à tout.

exEn: The old man is weak, but wise.
exFr: Le vieillard est faible, mais sage.

ex: Ὁ ἵππος ταχύς, ἡ δὲ χελώνη βραδεῖα.
exEn: The horse is fast, but the tortoise is slow.
exFr: Le cheval est rapide, mais la tortue est lente.

exEn: The tortoise, though slow, won.
exFr: La tortue, bien que lente, a gagné.

ex: Ῥᾴδιον τὸ λέγειν, χαλεπὸν δὲ τὸ ποιεῖν.
exEn: Saying is easy, doing is hard.
exFr: Dire est facile, faire est difficile.

exEn: It is difficult to know oneself.
exFr: Il est difficile de se connaître soi-même.

exEn: Learning is the sweetest thing for human beings.
exFr: Apprendre est pour les hommes la chose la plus douce.

exEn: War is sweet to those who have never tried it.
exFr: La guerre est douce pour qui ne l'a pas connue.

exEn: Truth is bitter to many.
exFr: La vérité est amère pour beaucoup.

exEn: The eagle's eye is sharp.
The road to wisdom is long.
exFr: Longue est la route vers la sagesse.

exEn: He says much in few words.
exFr: Il dit beaucoup en peu de mots.

exEn: Lightning strikes the heights.
The wise man is always rich.

ex: Ὁ πένης οὐδὲν φοβεῖται· οὐδὲν γὰρ ἔχει.
exEn: The poor man fears nothing, for he has nothing.
exFr: Le pauvre ne craint rien, car il n'a rien.

exEn: The free man has the right to speak openly.
exFr: L'homme libre a le droit de parler franchement.

exEn: What belongs to friends is held in common.

ex: Ὁ τὰ ἴδια μόνον σκοπῶν ἰδιώτης.
exEn: He who looks only to his own affairs is an idiotes.
exFr: Celui qui ne regarde que ses affaires privées est un idiotès.

ex: Πολλὰ τὰ δεινά, κοὐδὲν ἀνθρώπου δεινότερον.
exEn: Many things are wondrous, and none more wondrous than man.
exFr: Il est bien des merveilles, mais rien n'est plus prodigieux que l'homme.

exEn: Being mortal, think mortal thoughts.
exFr: Étant mortel, aie des pensées de mortel.

exEn: The soul is immortal.
This is clear to everyone.
Each one does his own work.
A good friend is worth much.
The strong do what they can.
exFr: Les puissants font ce qu'ils peuvent.

exEn: Snow is white.
The black earth gives fruit.
exFr: La terre noire donne ses fruits.

ex: Καθαρὸν ὕδωρ ἐκ τῆς πηγῆς ῥεῖ.
exEn: Pure water flows from the spring.
exFr: Une eau pure coule de la source.

exEn: The marketplace is full of people.

ex: Κενὸς ὁ λόγος ὃς οὐδὲν θεραπεύει.
exEn: Empty is the argument that heals nothing.
exFr: Vide est le discours qui ne guérit rien.

ex: Ὁ πρῶτος ἐν τῷ ἀγῶνι στέφανον λαμβάνει.
exEn: The first in the contest receives a crown.
exFr: Le premier du concours reçoit une couronne.

exEn: Like always draws near to like.

ex: Εἷς οἰωνὸς ἄριστος, ἀμύνεσθαι περὶ πάτρης.
exEn: One omen is best: to fight for one's country.
exFr: Un seul présage est le meilleur : combattre pour sa patrie.

ex: Μηδένα πρὸ τοῦ τέλους εὐδαίμονα κάλει.
exEn: Call no one happy before the end.
exFr: Ne dis personne heureux avant la fin.

ex: Ὅμηρος τυφλὸς ἦν, ἀλλὰ πάντα ἑώρα.
exEn: Homer was blind, but he saw everything.
exFr: Homère était aveugle, mais il voyait tout.

exEn: The temperate man rules his pleasures.

ex: Ὁ ἀνδρεῖος τοὺς κινδύνους οὐ φοβεῖται.
exEn: The brave man does not fear dangers.
exFr: L'homme courageux ne craint pas les dangers.

exEn: The coward dies many times.
Now is the moment.

ex: Τότε νέος ἦν, νῦν δὲ γέρων.
exEn: Then I was young, now I am old.
exFr: Alors j'étais jeune, maintenant je suis vieux.

exEn: God is always doing geometry.
exFr: Dieu fait toujours de la géométrie.

exEn: Truth never dies.
You often ask the same thing.
exFr: Tu demandes souvent la même chose.

exEn: Again and again we learn.
It is already evening.
Wait a little longer.
I am coming right away.
Time flees quickly.

ex: Οὐ τὸ ζῆν, ἀλλὰ τὸ εὖ ζῆν.
exEn: Not living, but living well.
exFr: Non pas vivre, mais bien vivre.

exEn: The liar has a bad reputation.
Well said.
It is very well.

ex: Μᾶλλον φιλῶ τὴν ἀλήθειαν ἢ τὴν δόξαν.
exEn: I love truth more than opinion.
exFr: J'aime la vérité plus que l'opinion.

exEn: Above all I honor wisdom.
So the matter stands.
I live here.

ex: Ἐκεῖ ἡ ἀγορά, ἐνθάδε τὸ ἱερόν.
exEn: There is the marketplace, here is the temple.
Where on earth am I?
How are you?
When will our friend arrive?

ex: Ἡ κώμη ἐγγὺς τῆς θαλάσσης ἐστίν.
exEn: The village is near the sea.
exFr: Le village est près de la mer.

exEn: He lives far from the city.
exFr: Il habite loin de la ville.

exEn: The rivers flow backwards (the world is upside down).
exFr: Les fleuves remontent vers leurs sources (le monde à l'envers).

exEn: Everything is turned upside down.
Today I am learning a new word.
Tomorrow will be better.

ex: Χθὲς ὗεν, σήμερον δὲ λάμπει ὁ ἥλιος.
exEn: Yesterday it rained, today the sun is shining.
exFr: Hier il pleuvait, aujourd'hui le soleil brille.

ex: Οἴκοι μένειν δεῖ τὸν καλῶς εὐδαίμονα.
exEn: He who would be truly happy should stay at home.
exFr: Qui veut être vraiment heureux doit rester chez soi.

exEn: Perhaps tomorrow we shall know.

ex: Οἱ ἀγροὶ ἔξω τῶν τειχῶν εἰσιν.
exEn: The fields are outside the walls.
exFr: Les champs sont hors des murs.

exEn: The master is inside.
Nothing in excess.
